pr_title: fix: Add XML definition node type
pr_body:
Adds a new node type for XML definitions. XML definition nodes are effectively the same as `NODE_ELEMENT`s except for the type itself.

Closes #72517
pr_comments: While I'm not sure about the usefulness of this PR (@timothyqiu noted that this isn't a full featured parser), I just want to point out that this PR is marked as ready for review and that there are some syntax errors, perhaps stemming from some refactoring. If you are still working on this I'd recommend marking this as a draft.

issue_context.title: `XMLParser` handles XML Declaration node incorrectly.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.beta16

### System information

Linux 5.15.89-1 x86_64 (Manjaro XFCE)

### Issue description

Take the following XML as an example:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<library>
    <book name="Pirates" genre="sci-fi" author="pew;" />
    <bookseries book_count="2">
        <book name="ABC" genre="education" author="also pew;" />
        <book name="DEF" genre="education" author="also pew;" />
    </bookseries>
</library>
```
According to the [spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-prolog-dtd), XML files begin with an XML declaration. When trying to parse it, Godot fails and gives `NodeType.NODE_UNKNOWN`, making a lot of the functions on `XMLParser` return invalid data. The core problem might be the nonexistence of something like `NodeType.NODE_XMLDECL`, but doesn't matter in most cases; an acceptable and convenient solution would be `XMLParser` treating XML declaration as an [empty element](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#dt-empty), but a separate node type would be nice too.

### Steps to reproduce

Try to parse the above XML and `print()` a few properties for the xml declaration node: you'll see a lot of weird and incorrect stuff, for example, `XMLParser.get_node_name()` returning `"?xml version="1.0" ..."`.

### Minimal reproduction project

[XMLParserIssue.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10558387/XMLParserIssue.zip)
comments:
It's intended that the declaration is ignored and marked as `NODE_UNKNOWN` (as there is no suitable category for it).

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0a9e6e478e3183d7bf3c5cb895c706bc6275d3ea/core/io/xml_parser.cpp#L322-L324

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0a9e6e478e3183d7bf3c5cb895c706bc6275d3ea/core/io/xml_parser.cpp#L92-L105

The unwanted function behavior is documented. e.g. `get_node_name()` only makes sense when the current node is an element node. But it's indeed wrong that the function did not print an error when you try to call it.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0a9e6e478e3183d7bf3c5cb895c706bc6275d3ea/doc/classes/XMLParser.xml#L58-L63

> It's intended that the declaration is ignored and marked as `NODE_UNKNOWN` (as there is no suitable category for it).
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0a9e6e478e3183d7bf3c5cb895c706bc6275d3ea/core/io/xml_parser.cpp#L322-L324
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0a9e6e478e3183d7bf3c5cb895c706bc6275d3ea/core/io/xml_parser.cpp#L92-L105
> 
> The unwanted function behavior is documented. e.g. `get_node_name()` only makes sense when the current node is an element node. But it's indeed wrong that the function did not print an error when you try to call it.
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0a9e6e478e3183d7bf3c5cb895c706bc6275d3ea/doc/classes/XMLParser.xml#L58-L63

I believe there should at least be a workaround for getting xmldecl's attributes (some may want to check for `version` or `encoding` or whatever defined there). Replacing `?`s with `""` and ` /` before parsing is not really reliable.

@ItsAleph What's your use case for obtaining XML version and/or encoding?

XMLParser is not a full-featured parser. It won't do anything according to these information. e.g. It assumes the input is UTF-8 encoded. So you won't be able to handle a misencoded document with XMLParser even if you get the right encoding from XML declaration.

For me personally this is not a need, but i am working on add-on that provides support for high-level manipulation of XML data (reading, dumping, beautifying and conversion to dict) and i want to make sure i cover the needs of as much users as possible.

Bumped on this in Godot 4.0.3. 
I assumed the expected behavior was as the code expects in doctool, which I was following as an example:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/329652b6feac2114c4e30062f18ece36d4e3addc/editor/doc_tools.cpp#L1176-L1185

But instead I get `NODE_UNKNOWN` and `get_node_name()` returns `?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>` without the opening `<`.

`doctool` gets away with it because later it has a fallback for `NODE_UNKNOWN`, so wasn't noticeable.

review_comments: I'd move `NODE_XML_DEFINITION` before `NODE_UNKNOWN`, but I'm not completely sure whether it's good practice around here.
